novelty.justification: The claim proposes that models “spontaneously embed these entities in a representation subspace whose geometry is isomorphic to the true relational structure” and that this geometry “predicts the model's downstream generalization,” so its novelty route is a cross-domain ontology-geometry measurement linked to generalization rather than a wholly new target phenomenon. Searches using “language model embeddings periodic table,” “chemical embeddings recover periodic table,” “protein language model embeddings phylogeny,” and “representation geometry ontology generalization” identify close precedents: Zhou et al., “Learning atoms for materials discovery” (Atom2Vec, 2018) recovered chemically meaningful organization of elements from compound co-occurrence; Tshitoyan et al., “Unsupervised word embeddings capture latent knowledge from materials science literature” (2019) recovered materials-science relationships; and Rives et al., “Biological structure and function emerge from scaling unsupervised learning to 250 million protein sequences” (2021) showed evolutionary and functional organization in protein-model representations. Extending those established embedding analyses to canonical lattices, trees, and taxonomies with a combined “Relational-Fidelity Score” and correlating fidelity with held-out generalization is a non-trivial systematic integration, but it is a natural extension rather than a new core relationship or measurement paradigm.
